haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first, in one transaction with the change and a users_pg_pending upsert. Then a safe copy to PG runs with a 500 ms timeout. A PG failure does not fail the request; the outbox row stays.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the incoming version is higher than the stored PG row's version, and the id is not in PG's users_tombstones.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance must be confirmed on dual_mysql_primary, then at least one more minute. Instances can disagree for up to 30s after a flag change.
haiku-low.q4: It reads the MySQL replica, copies at most 2,000 rows per batch in id order, and sleeps whenever mysql_replica_lag_seconds exceeds 5.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: a full checker pass with 0 mismatches, then the 1/10/50/100 ramp. Source of truth: reads 100% on PG for 3+ days, last night's checker clean, at a quiet time.
haiku-low.q6: The users_pg_pending outbox row in MySQL, written in the same transaction as the change. The MySQL-side sweeper re-copies to PG within about 15s, or once PG is back.
haiku-low.q7: Copies and deletes take a per-id lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock in PG, locking read on users_tombstones in MySQL). Deletes write tombstones in both DBs, and copies skip tombstoned ids.
haiku-low.q8: In PG's users_backfill_progress row (last_copied_id, target_max_id), updated in the same PG transaction as each batch. It stops when no rows remain at or below target_max_id.
haiku-low.q9: The checker compares both DBs 10,000 ids at a time. It rechecks differences on the source-of-truth primary 5s later, pushes survivors to that DB's outbox, and reports a mismatch count per pass.
haiku-low.q10: Every instance must show frozen before writes resume, so none writes MySQL-first while another writes PG-first. If not finished by T0+60s, flip to dual_mysql_primary and retry another day.
haiku-low.q11: MySQL assigns ids until cutover. After cutover, PG's identity assigns them, restarted above MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT. After a rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set past PG's next identity value.
haiku-low.q12: Every PG write is outboxed to MySQL and repaired, and nightly checks push mismatches there. Rollback: freeze, empty the outbox, bump AUTO_INCREMENT, then set dual_mysql_primary and read_from_pg=0. The option ends at pg_only retirement, at least 14 days after cutover.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first: one MySQL transaction does the change and upserts the users_pg_pending outbox row; commit means the write is done. Then a safe copy into PG (500 ms timeout), then the outbox row is removed if the token matches. If PG fails or times out, the request does NOT fail; the outbox row stays and the sweeper fixes PG.
sonnet.q2: Only when the incoming version is higher than the existing row's version (safe copy: skip tombstoned ids, insert if missing, overwrite only if incoming version is higher).
sonnet.q3: Every instance must be confirmed on write_mode dual_mysql_primary, then wait at least another minute. Instances can disagree for up to 30s after a flag change (they refresh flags every 30s).
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica (not the primary), in id order, at most 2,000 rows per batch, and sleeps whenever mysql_replica_lag_seconds > 5. (Only target_max_id is read from the primary, once at start.)
sonnet.q5: Reads to PG: the checker has done a full clean pass (0 mismatches) after the backfill finishes; then ramp read_from_pg 1/10/50/100 holding at least an hour each with PG read errors and p99 within MySQL's. Source of truth switch (cutover): reads at 100% PG for at least 3 days, last night's checker run clean, at a quiet time.
sonnet.q6: The users_pg_pending outbox row (user_id plus token), kept in MySQL, written in the same transaction as the user change so it survives a crash. The MySQL-side sweeper/catch-up worker (wakes every 10s, takes rows older than 5s, re-reads the current row from the MySQL primary, safe-copies into PG, deletes the outbox row if the token is unchanged) brings PG back in line, about 15s, or once PG is back.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: every delete writes the id into users_tombstones in both DBs in the same transaction as removing the row; safe copy skips ids in the target's tombstones. A per-id lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock(id) in PG, a locking read of the id in users_tombstones in MySQL) taken by both copy and delete prevents interleaving.
sonnet.q8: In the PG table users_backfill_progress (one row: last_copied_id and target_max_id), written in the same PG transaction as each batch, so a failed batch rolls back with its progress and a crash resumes from last_copied_id. It stops when a read finds no rows left at or below target_max_id (max(id) read on the MySQL primary at start).
sonnet.q9: The checker/comparer: it goes through both DBs 10,000 ids at a time comparing id, version and a hash of other columns, reading the MySQL replica (pausing when lag > 5s). Each difference is re-checked against the source-of-truth primary 5s later, and those that remain are pushed into the outbox in the source-of-truth DB (for the sweeper to fix); it reports a mismatch count per pass.
sonnet.q10: write_mode is set to frozen; the cutover waits until every instance shows frozen in app_flag_value (up to 30s) plus 5s for the write deadline, so no instance writes in the interim; then dual_pg_primary is set. If not finished by T0+60s, flip to dual_mysql_primary instead (nothing to undo; try another day). Total pause stays at or under 90s (60s cutoff plus 30s flag refresh).
sonnet.q11: PG's identity column (GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY) assigns new ids. At cutover it is restarted at n = MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT counter read on the primary (above every id MySQL ever issued, including erased ones in tombstones). Copies to MySQL use explicit ids, dragging MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT past them. On rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set to PG identity's next value so it can't reissue an id PG gave out.
sonnet.q12: During PG-primary, each write commits in PG with a users_mysql_pending outbox upsert, then safe-copies to MySQL (explicit id, 500 ms timeout) and removes the outbox row if the token matches; if the copy fails, the PG-side repair worker fixes MySQL. Rollback (PG must be reachable): freeze at a new T0 (frozen, confirmed, plus 5s), wait for users_mysql_pending to be empty, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to PG identity's next value, then set write_mode=dual_mysql_primary and read_from_pg=0; if not done by T0+60s, revert to dual_pg_primary and try later. Pause at most 90s. The option ends at pg_only (after at least 14 days since cutover with no rollback and a clean nightly pass), the point of no return, since MySQL then misses data.
